subject: part
title: (R)PART.------POL.DY.
description: Diagram in PCC-17, paired with v1-p333-1. (R)PART (the reality of participation) is crossed with POL-DYM (political dynamics). The diagram poses what *real* participation requires when crossed with political dynamics in the post-Cage context where MEV's 'sound pool' (audience-participating communal music) was one experimental answer. PART → EXP-DYM (expansion dynamics); RT-DY (reality dynamics) → EXP-DYM; PROG-SIGN (progressional significance) → EXP-DYM. EXP-DYM is the central hub — three independent feeds. EXP-DYM → ALT-C-PG (alternative composite progressionalism) and EXP-DYM → INFO-DS (information dissemination). A separate chain: ACC-DY (accelerated dynamics) → POL-DYM → EXP-INFO-B (expansion information basis). Structural argument: real participation, reality dynamics, and progressional significance converge on expansion dynamics — a triple-feed hub — and from there produce alternative composite progressionalism and information dissemination. The political-dynamics chain runs in parallel: accelerated dynamics produces political dynamics, which produces expansion-information-basis. The two halves of the diagram run *in parallel* without converging — meaning real participation's productive outputs (alt-c-pg and info-ds) and political-dynamics' productive outputs (expansion-information-basis) are separate, not derived from each other. The crossing is structurally a *parallel* not a *convergent* one — Braxton's diagrammatic statement that real participation does not depend on political dynamics for its expansion.
